datasets.experimentTitle: Bed Rest Standard Measures:  Acetaminophen Test
datasets.description: This dataset contains data for all Campaign 1 subjects for the Bed Rest Standard Measure Acetaminophen (BRSMAcet) study. Data collection sessions for this measure were performed once pre-bed rest, three times during bed rest, and one time post bed rest. Urine, blood, saliva, and breath samples were taken during the data collection sessions to determine the absorption rate of acetaminophen. The Analyzed Data folder contains maximal concentration, half life, and observed volume and clearance of acetaminophen derived from saliva samples for each subject who completed the study.

datasets.experimentTitle: Bed Rest Standard Measures:  Acetaminophen Test

Data collection sessions for this measure were performed once pre-bed rest, three times during bed rest, and one time post bed rest. Urine, blood, saliva, and breath samples were taken during the data collection sessions to determine the absorption rate of acetaminophen. Data in this dataset includes maximal concentration, half life, and Area Under Concentration time curve derived from saliva samples.

This dataset contains data for all Campaign 1 subjects for the Bed Rest Standard Measure Actigraphy (BRSMAct) study. Sleep variables were measured using wrist actigraphy before bed rest, during bed rest, and post bed rest. Mean values of sleep latency, sleep duration, and sleep efficiency are provided for BR-2 through BR+6. The data generated by the actigraph were analyzed for the sleep-wake cycle, the quality of rest, and sleep to wake ratio. The Analyzed Data folder contains mean values for sleep latency, sleep duration, and sleep efficiency.

datasets.experimentTitle: Bed Rest Standard Measures: Plasma Volume
datasets.description: This dataset includes data collected from Bed Rest Standard Measure Plasma Volume experiment on the Lunar Analog Feasibility Study (LAFS) Phase 1 Study and the LAFSP2, Phase 2 Study. The study was divided into campaign segments. This media contains the following campaigns: LAFS (05/13/2008 - 0606/2008), LAFS2 (07/08/20085 - 12/19/2008, LAFS3 (09/09/2008 - 12/09/2008, and LAFSP2 (04/20/2008 - 08/27/2008). During the LAFS operations, subjects wore special support stockings on their legs (Jobst® stockings). During LAFS Phase 1 session one, subjects wore thigh high stockings with 30-40mmHg of compression, session two, subjects wore thigh high stockings with 36-46mmHg of compression and session three, subjects wore knee high stockings at 36-46mmHg of compression. The results from this study will be combined with the results from the Cleveland Clinic Foundation study, The bedrest (BR) portion of this study was conducted at the UTMB GCRC for a period of six days. Subjects remained in a 9.5-degree head-up position to simulate 1/6th gravity loading on the feet.

description:
Changes in serum sclerostin and bone turnover markers in healthy adult men undergoing controlled bed rest were determined. Seven healthy adult men (31 ± 3 yr old) underwent 90 days of 6 degree head down tilt bed rest at the University of Texas Medical Branch Institute for Translational Sciences-Clinical Research Center.

Serum sclerostin, PTH, vitamin D, bone resorption and formation markers, urinary calcium and phosphorus excretion, and 24-h pooled urinary markers of bone resorption were evaluated before bed rest [baseline (BL)] and at bed rest d 28 (BR-28), d 60 (BR-60), and d 90 (BR-90). Bone mineral density was measured at BL, BR-60, and 5 d after the end of the study (BR+5).

Bone mineral density declined significantly (1-2% per month) at weight-bearing skeletal sites. Serum sclerostin was elevated above BL at BR-28 (+29 ± 20%; P = 0.003) and BR-60 (+42 ± 31%; P < 0.001), with a lesser increase at BR-90 (+22 ± 21%; P = 0.07). Serum PTH levels were reduced at BR-28 (-17 ± 16%; P = 0.02) and BR-60 (-24 ± 14%; P = 0.03) and remained lower than BL at BR-90 (-21 ± 21%; P = 0.14), but did not reach statistical significance. Serum bone turnover markers were unchanged; however, urinary bone resorption markers and calcium were significantly elevated at all time points after bed rest (P < 0.01).

datasets.datasetName: Nutritional Status Assessment Before, During, and After Long-Duration Head-Down Bed Rest
description:
This article summarizes the nutritional status from 13 subjects participating in 60 or 90 days of head down bed rest. Graphs and tables in the article are as follows: (1) markers of bone metabolism, (2) vitamins, (3) markers of oxidative damage and antioxidants, (4) urine chemistry, (5) blood chemistry, and (6) hematology and iron status before, during, and after bed rest.

Source: Zwart SR, Oliver SAM, Fesperman JV, Kala G, Krauhs J, Ericson K, Smith SM. Nutritional status assessment before, during, and after long-duration head-down bed rest. Aviat Space Environ Med 2009; 80(5,Suppl.):A15-22.

The main objective was to assess testosterone and hormone status in long- and short-duration space flight and bed rest environments and to determine relationships with other physiological systems, including bone and muscle. Blood and urine samples were collected before, during, and after long-duration space flight. Samples were also collected before and after 12- to 14-d missions and from participants in 30- to 90-d bed rest studies. Space flight studies were conducted on the International Space Station and before and after Space Shuttle missions. Bed rest studies were conducted in a clinical research center setting. Data from Skylab missions are also presented.

All of the participants were male, and they included 15 long-duration and nine short-duration mission crew members and 30 bed rest subjects. Serum total, free, and bioavailable testosterone were measured along with serum and urinary cortisol, serum dehydroepiandrosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, and SHBG. Total, free, and bioavailable testosterone was not changed during long-duration space flight but were decreased (P < 0.01) on landing day after these flights and after short-duration space flight. There were no changes in other hormones measured. Testosterone concentrations dropped before and soon after bed rest, but bed rest itself had no effect on testosterone. There was no evidence for decrements in testosterone during long-duration space flight or bed rest.

datasets.experimentTitle: Human Cerebral Cortex Plasticity in Response to Long-term Bedrest as an Analog to Microgravity
description:
This final report summarizes results for Cerebral Cortex Plasticity After 90 Days of Bed Rest, experiment NNJ04HF70G.

Data summarized in the paper are as follows:

  • Timeline of study showing the data collection points for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), functional MRI (fMRI), and functional mobility testing (FMT)
  • Linearity of the transformed recruitment curves
  • Linear model fits of the recruitment curves across measurement periods
  • Means and standard errors of the log motor evoked potential (MEP) values across all study measurement periods
  • Log motor evoked potentials (MEP) correlated with maze performance data
  • Example of fMRI activation patterns
  • fMRI percent signal change for single voxel with highest z value
  • Map of estimated local displacements between scans displayed on the first timepoint scan
  • Enlarged views of 1st and 2nd scans together with the estimated local volume change between the two, shown as a gray scale % change.
  • Statistics showing the 8 subjects' volume change maps transformed to a common template
